To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the roles of innate and acquired immunity in HTLV-1 infection are critical for the pathogenesis of HTLV- 1-associated diseases.

HTLV-1 infection induces a type-I IFN and a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response in HTLV-1-carriers, and that the balance of these responses determines the status of HTVL-1-infected T-cells and the development of ATL and HTLV- 1- associated myelopathy/tropica spastic parapresis.
HTLV-1 infection induces type-I IFN and IFN-inducible genes in HTLV-1 carrier cells in vivo, and that HTLV-2 infection does not induce type-I IFN responses in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the roles of acquired and intrinsic immunity in the pathogenesis of HTLV- 1-associated diseases.
the roles of acquired and natural immunity in the pathogenesis and prevention of HTLV- 1-associated diseases.
the roles of acquired and/or innate immunity in the pathogenesis and development of ATL and/or HTLV-1- associated myelopathy/tropic spastic paraparasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HTLV-1 infection is a complex process in which both the innate and acquired immune responses play important roles.
the roles of innate and acquired immunity in the pathogenesis of HTLV- 1-mediated diseases are complex and remain to be clarified.
HTLV-1 infection induces both acquired and innate immune activation and responses, and these are the important determinants of HTLV- 1-mediated diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the balance between HTLV-1 replication, host immune responses and the host environment determines the outcome of HTLV- 1 infection.
both innate and acquired immune responses are important in the pathogenesis of HTLV- 1-mediated diseases.
the host immune response to HTLV-1 plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of HTLV- 1-associated diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system can play an active role in HTLV-1 disease pathogenesis and progression.
the host defense mechanisms against HTLV-1 infection are complex and involve a variety of immune responses.
the immune system plays a key role in controlling the HTLV-1 infection and in preventing the development of HTL-1-mediated diseases.
